title: What would be the best native resolution?

posts.author: Ingwer
posts.body:
This crossed my thoughts from time to time, but recently it occurred to me that the answer isn't actually that simple.
I always hoped for the next main line iteration to "finally support high resolution natively" - meaning all assets and interfaces are automatically provided for a 16:9 HD experience.
Now, with RPG Maker Unite on the horizon, it seems that we are even getting more than that, as it will support Full HD natively (from what I could gather out of their Devlog).
So - this is great, right? Who wouldn't like to have bigger and better resolutions baked into the software to keep up with modern hardware? But this is where I think it actually becomes a bit problematic.
If we look at the comparison of SD (what RPG Maker up to MZ basically uses by default) to HD (not Full HD) - then yes, I think it would be great. While not saying everyone and their grandchildren have a device using HD resolution, the amount of users still having SD monitors in any way "should" be very low by now - and even for some time. So I guess one can safely call HD an implemented standard by now.
For Full HD however, this isn't the case. There is a big range of price segments where a device you'll get will not have a FHD display. The price may have been lowered since its introduction, but most of the time, it is still at least in the higher mid-range for a device to offer such resolution.
This is of course where the supposed "default" user base splits. People who enjoy playing the latest AAA titles will probably have a computer (and/or monitor) that supports FHD - solely based on meeting the rest of the necessary hardware requirements. But there is a good, solid group of users who use lower- and mid-range devices which simply don't offer that.
And why would they need devices with FHD? To play 2D/RPG Maker games? When would these games request such high hardware to be able to run them?
Sure, each iteration has upped the requirements, and increasing the overall resolution and graphical quality will increase this as well. Also, depending on what 2D/RPG Maker game you are actually playing, you may have varying results. Still, I would say it's pretty sure to assume that you shouldn't need a higher mid- to lower end- tier device to run them.
With that being said - what happens if you combine a (potential) user base for your game with a native Full HD resolution as the bare minimum? It get's complicated.
Sure, they can play your game - after all, when resizing the application to fit your screen, the game will be completely visible. But if your display does not have a high enough resolution, everything will shrink down to fit in the lower amount of pixels - resulting in a lowered quality and/or harder to view experience (so: not the intended experience when you made your game).
Again, if this would be a neglectable amount of users, you would probably just live with it (or rather they have to) - but it is not only a good amount of the total user base, it may also be the biggest part of user base your game will get. So you would probably like to get these players the intended experience for your game. Which means Full HD is not what you are looking for.
So, what do you do? Because as of now, RPG Maker does not offer full support for switching resolutions (and Unite will neither from what I could tell). This means you will always have to work (around) on your project before you even started it.
While working on your project is not the problem itself (because that's what you have to do normally) - it begs the question if offering a Full HD resolution as native minimum is the best idea in this environment. Wouldn't it be better to do it the other way around - offering HD as minimum and offering Full HD as an option if you put in the work?
There are also other things to mention. Namely assets. Currently, a lot of artists focusing on working to support RPG Maker devs are offering their work in the quality the software offers. (There are exceptions of course). But in general, if an artist before capped his work at the default software resolution (SD), they obviously have to increase their effort in some way to make an HD product. This of course results in... well, different results. Maybe an asset pack with fewer graphics, a piece of art with less details - or the same product for a higher price.
While I'm not against paying a higher price for "higher" art - the question arises if FHD isn't overdoing it - making it unnecessarily cumbersome for both artist and game dev. (Of course this is debatable, especially if you are looking to make a FHD game).
That being said, this whole question is of course debatable - and one is also free to just "want" FHD because they would like to make a game with it. From an objective point of view (although it is still only my perspective), I find it doubtful if setting such a resolution as native minimum is the best way to go forward, though.
So, what is your opinion on this? Do you think HD or Full HD would be great for the next main line iteration? Or maybe you think they should stick with SD for some reasons? Or maybe they should "just" add support to easily adjust and add assets for different resolutions?
Also, I am known for thinking the wrong way around when it comes to resolutions. So maybe I missed something or am completely wrong? Feel free to correct me or add your point of view.
Thanks for reading.

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
So, even though it's in Unity, which comes with some really nice tools for making UI that can easily scale to multiple resolutions, Unite will not have that support? That's a shame.
I guess FHD is probably the most future-proof resolution if you're just focusing on one - especially since we're not targeting current hardware, but hardware that will exist when Unite games are done.
And it does seems to go for more high-res look in general, looking at the 96x96 assets we've seen. So the engine is specialising, so to speak - more retro-styled games might be better done in MV/MZ, but if you want something more high-res then Unite would be better suited for it.

posts.author: Ingwer
posts.body:
Mac15001900 said:
So, even though it's in Unity, which comes with some really nice tools for making UI that can easily scale to multiple resolutions, Unite will not have that support? That's a shame.
Click to expand...
That is true. The editor interface is quite different from the main line versions - so adjusting stuff like UI is (hopefully) easier and more flexible.
From what I've seen however (again, correct me if I'm wrong), the editor in general does not seem to give you much more freedom compared to before. If you, for example, set faces, you are (probably) still bound to the software telling you "I use x by x pixels as maximum resolution. Now something like face-sets can of course be work-arounded - but that means the software does (and will) not flexible change its scales and such depending on what resolution you are going for.

posts.author: bigsmiles
posts.body:
I feel like it depends on your goal. For example if mass commercial success is the aim, then needing to search for statistics about what majority game consumers use as resolution. It would not really matter at all about the rest of consumers, from an economic business standpoint.
If paying homage and catering to an audience who prefer a certain type, then that type.
For me the best solution would be when making new project - "HD? SD?" choice at initial creation. I can't imagine it is such a difficult possibility. Assets etc are a different issue, the user can have the problem of locating or creating those.
For example it'd be pretty nifty if new RPG Maker had a simple option for "Create HD Project, Create Retro Project."

posts.author: aceherlechin
posts.body:
You bring up some interesting points, but it's actually not true that working in HD is more difficult for artists. With sharp, clear graphics, you can use an actual drawing for a tile or sprite. With the graphics unnaturally scaled back to a retro look, only pixel art is viable, and not all artists can work in pixels.
Now that a year has passed and we've learned that RPG Maker Unite was just a buggy cash grab, what are the chances we'll get an HD capable version of RPG Maker?
